header.running_head: The Fervour of the Sahabah (RA) to earn Rewards

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdul Jabbaar bin Haarith (RA) Seeks rewards for his Companionship with Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdul Jabbaar bin Haarith bin Maalik Hadasi Manaari (RA)
blocks.text:
Hadhrat Abdul Jabbaar bin Haarith bin Maalik Hadasi Manaari (RA) narrates, "I was part of a delegation to Rasulullaah ﷺ from the land of Saraat. When I came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, I greeted him with the traditional Arab greeting saying, 'May you have a good morning!' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Allaah has given Muhammad ﷺ and his Ummah another greeting. They greet each other with the words of Salaam.' I then said: 'اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَسُوْلَ اللّٰهِ'. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied by saying, 'وَعَلَيْكَ السَّلَامُ'. When he asked what my name was, I informed him that I was Jabbaar bin Haarith. I then accepted Islaam and pledge my allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ. After I had pledge my allegiance someone said to Rasulullaah ﷺ. 'This Manaari is one of the accomplished horsemen of his tribe.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then gave me a horse and I remained fighting by his side.
When Rasulullaah ﷺ one day missed the neighing of the horse he had given me, he asked, 'Why do I not hear the neighing of the Hadasi's horse?' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' I explained, 'I was told that its neighing was disturbing you so I had it castrated (to quieten it).' It was then that Rasulullaah ﷺ forbade castrating horses. Someone once suggested to me to request Rasulullaah ﷺ for a note (of guaranteeing for something) as my cousin Tameem Daari (RA) had done. 'Did he ask for something of this world or for something of the Aakhirah?' I asked. When I was told that it was for something of this world, I said, 'It was from this world that I have turned away. I shall rather ask Rasulullaah ﷺ to assist me tomorrow when I appear before Allaah.'"[^1]
The Statement of Rasulullaah ﷺ Concerning Hadhrat Amr bin Taghlib (RA) and Hadhrat Amr (RA)'s Response

Hadhrat Amr bin Taghlib (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ gave something to some people and not to others, it appeared as if they were upset. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "I give to some people only for fear of their impatience and agitation. Then there are those whom I hand over to the goodness and independence Allaah has placed in their hearts. Amongst these people is Amr bin Taghlib." Hadhrat Amr bin Taghlib (RA) said, "I would not trade these words of Rasulullaah ﷺ even for red camels."[^2]
